note: Famous electric piano tracks. Each confirmed 2026-11-26 by YouTube's oEmbed (title and channel as it gave them). `start` = a starting setting on this site's model (EPiano), the page's own.

videos.title: The Doors - Riders on the Storm (Official Audio)
videos.does: Ray Manzarek played a Mark I Stage 73 in the studio (Wikipedia). Soft, rainy chords and a jazzy line, with no bark.

videos.title: Angela (Theme From Taxi)
videos.does: Wikipedia names it among Rhodes recordings. A bell-like melody over chords: the tine's attack is the point.

videos.title: Billy Joel - Just the Way You Are (Official Audio)
videos.does: Wikipedia does not name this song; it is widely called a Rhodes record (unverified). Soft chords with a slow, gentle movement.

videos.title: The Logical Song
videos.does: Wikipedia names Supertramp's Wurlitzer on it. Bouncy, bright chords with a little bite.

videos.title: Dreamer
videos.does: Also named by Wikipedia. A fast repeated chord figure: hard hits that bark.

videos.title: Queen - You're My Best Friend (Official Video)
videos.does: John Deacon played the Wurlitzer (Wikipedia). A steady comping part under the voices.

videos.title: Bill Withers - Use Me (Official Audio)
videos.does: Wikipedia names it. A two-note groove that never lets go: short, damped notes.

videos.title: Higher Ground
videos.does: Wikipedia names it. A driving riff, thick and gritty (on the record also through effects: unverified).

videos.title: Genesis - That's All (Official Music Video)
videos.does: Tony Banks's CP-70 (Wikipedia). A bouncing chord part, bright and percussive.

videos.title: Peter Gabriel - In Your Eyes
videos.does: Wikipedia names it. Chords that ring and shimmer under the voice.

videos.title: The Zombies - She's Not There (Mono Remastered) (Official Lyric Video)
videos.does: Wikipedia names it. The famous keyboard solo and the soft, clipped chords.

videos.title: The Guess Who - These Eyes (Official Audio)
videos.does: Wikipedia names it. Gentle chords under the verse.
